observation_reviews.rationale: The 2023-03-31 fix itself matches the page (term loan '6.25 % PIK 11.06 % PIK', tag InterestRatePaidInKind 0.1106; revolver printed without PIK), but the observation treats this as a one-quarter row defect and its detection decision covers only that shape. The same loan prints the identical shape one quarter later ('S + 6.25 % PIK 11.35 % PIK', 0001885968-23-000025) and every later quarter ('S + 6.25 % PIK 9.92 %'), and rftsb publishes those with pik_rate 6.25 (the margin) and interest_rate_cash 3.67 to 5.36. So after the fix one Applitools quarter reads the whole coupon as PIK and the next eleven read only the margin. Par accretion decides it: 6,827 -> 7,023 -> 7,229 -> 7,443 (+2.9 pct a quarter, the full 11.06-11.35 coupon over 4, not the 1.56 pct margin), and 7,966 -> 8,164 -> 8,369 in 2026 (+2.5 pct, the full 9.92). Fund-wide (pik_margin.py on rftsb): 55 loan rows, $253.6M fair value, publish pik_rate equal to the spread below the rate; on 39 chain steps 28 accrete nearer the full coupon than the margin (Applitools, Sweep Purchaser 'S + 5.75 % PIK', FPG, KWOR). This is a systematic PIK-leg reading, not a row defect, and it affects the published PIK figures. Next action: widen this observation to the fund's 'S + x % PIK' reading, decide (fund agent, or owner if it is a convention question) whether pik_rate should be the whole coupon, and propose a check comparing pik_rate with par accretion; until then this observation's coverage and detection decision are incomplete.
